brief:
Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud of intentionally delaying coalition negotiations, according to Al Jazeera English. Eisenkot alleged the move was designed to force Israel toward another election while the outgoing government remains in power.

The accusation reflects deepening tensions in coalition formation talks following recent Israeli elections. Eisenkot's criticism suggests growing frustration among potential coalition partners over the pace and direction of negotiations with Likud.
dek: Yashar party chief says Likud wants to drag Israel into another election under the outgoing government.
title: Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu's Likud of deliberately stalling coalition talks
